item.title: BCC commissions $1m road equipment
item.description: The Bulawayo City Council (BCC) has commissioned road construction and maintenance equipment worth more than US$1m, in a move aimed at strengthening its ability to rehabilitate the city’s deteriorating road network using in-house teams.

item.title: Chivayo pledges $1 million to Zimbabwe cricket team
item.description: He says it’s reward for qualifying to the Top Eights

item.title: RBZ Orders Removal Of Account Balance Inquiry, Cash Deposit Charges
item.description: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (RBZ) has taken steps to curb excessive cash withdrawal and point-of-sale (POS) charges imposed by financial institutions.

item.title: RBZ Unveils New ZiG Banknotes To Circulate From 7 April
item.description: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (RBZ) has unveiled a new series of Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG) banknotes, set to enter circulation on 7 April 2026.

item.title: Church leaders condemn amendment bill as threat to constitutional integrity
item.description: Church leaders have declared their firm opposition to the proposed Constitution of Zimbabwe (Amendment) Bill No. 3 of 2026, warning that the changes would fundamentally alter the spirit of the country’s people-driven 2013 Constitution and risk concentrating power at the expense of citizens’ voices.

item.title: Zimbabweans lured to Russia’s War: Inside the deceptive recruitment network drawing civilians to the frontlines
item.description: A growing network of recruiters operating in Zimbabwe and across southern Africa is drawing young men into Russia’s war in Ukraine through promises of civilian jobs and financial security, only for ‘many’ to find themselves on an active, deadly frontline war zone after minimal training.

item.title: Mpilo Hospital seeks new Chief Medical Officer
item.description: The Ministry of Health and Child Care has advertised several senior positions in its latest internal vacancy circulars, including the substantive post of Chief Medical Officer (CMO) at Mpilo Central Hospital in Bulawayo.

item.title: Rising anger over ‘lop-sided’ and ‘immoral’ US health funding pacts with African countries
item.description: Zimbabwe refuses to sign agreement and Kenya faces a court case over data sharing as new aid deals come under scrutiny

item.title: Zimbabwe’s processing for white gold deepens with another sulphate plant
item.description: Construction for another lithium sulphate plant in Zimbabwe has begun, as demand for lithium globally continues to surge.

item.title: Can Jonathan Moyo worm his way back to sideline “ED2030” proponents and reset the succession race?
item.description: In the world of power, there are those whose only true loyalty is to themselves.
